incident-bot: P1 alert: runtime-prod-1 pod OOMs detected across GPU pool us-west-2. Error rate spike -> customer-facing 504s. Paging @ryan :rotating_light:
ryan (oncall): acked. I'm on it. what services impacted? any customer reports?
jamie (cust-succ): we've seen 3 customer tickets referencing timeouts on embeddings and generation endpoints since 10:11 UTC. one escalated.
anne (sre): I'm pulling logs now, starting with pod restart traces and OOM killer logs.
eli (infra): infra alert shows high GPU mem fragmentation across nodes g0,g1. wondering if kv-cache growth + continuous batching triggered it.
maya (runtime-ml): adding context: same model (open-llama-33b-quant) on several nodes. KV cache per-request size + long context requests could provoke fragmentation.
ryan (oncall): runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oom-runtime. steps: 1) dump pod logs 2) get nvidia-smi and dmesg 3) check KV cache metrics 4) consider disabling kv-cache per-model.
anne (sre): running: kubectl -n runtime-prod logs runtime-prod-1 --since=15m > /tmp/runtime-prod-1.logs.txt
anne (sre): paste: ```OOMKilled process pid=8743 python3 /srv/runtime/server.py: Allocation failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/server.py", line 210, in handle_request
    output = model.generate(...)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory.```
eli (infra): nvidia-smi snapshot: ```+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12   Driver Version: 525.85.12   CUDA Version: 12.1     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  A100-SXM4-40GB    Off      | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  PID   Type   Process name                             Usage      |
| 8743   C      python3                                     39Gi / 40Gi |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+```
maya (runtime-ml): also pulled allocator stats from runtime metrics: ```gpu_total=40Gi gpu_free=1Gi gpu_allocated=39Gi fragmentation_ratio=0.28 kv_cache_bytes=6.7Gi batching_backlog=128 active_requests=42```
ryan (oncall): fragmentation_ratio 0.28 is high but not extreme. KV cache at 6.7Gi seems large for 40Gi device. can we temporarily disable KV cache for that model?
maya (runtime-ml): yes. we can flip model config via control plane: POST /models/open-llama-33b-quant/config {"kv_cache_enabled":false} — doing that now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: model-config-update open-llama-33b-quant -> kv_cache_enabled:false by maya at 1792345742
anne (sre): while config flips, reduce continuous batch size to 1 for the pool to avoid aggregated allocations: kubectl -n runtime-prod set env ds/runtime-workers BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512 BATCH_MAX_ITEMS=1
eli (infra): warning: reducing batch will increase latency/requests per GPU. good for mitigation.
ryan (oncall): make sure to adjust autoscaler threshold too if burst load expected.
maya (runtime-ml): kv-cache flip completed. telemetry shows kv_cache_bytes -> 1.1Gi in 40s.
ryan (oncall): any immediate improvement in OOMs?
anne (sre): pod runtime-prod-1 restarted at 1792345801 by kube; new instance running. checking logs for OOM after change.
anne (sre): new nvidia-smi: ```python process now using 28Gi / 40Gi```
jamie (cust-succ): customer tickets still report occasional 504s but volume down from 18/min to 2/min. reporting to customers: hold message drafted.
ryan (oncall): good. mark mitigation: kv-cache toggled off + batching reduced. we need an in-thread RCA draft.
eli (infra): collecting node-level slab/allocator fragmentation: `/proc/driver/nvidia/allocator_stats` shows large free chunks but scattered, causing large single-allocation failures.
maya (runtime-ml): hypothesis A: KV cache keeps large contiguous chunks pinned across requests; combined with variable-sized request allocations (long input contexts) threads request large contiguous blocks -> allocator can't find big enough block despite free total memory -> OOM.
maya (runtime-ml): hypothesis B: continuous batching with large batch backlog created many concurrent KV cache pointers in GPU memory preventing coalescing -> fragmentation.
anne (sre): evidence supporting A: kv_cache_bytes peaked before OOM each time in previous 40 minutes. logs: ```[10:09:41] kv_cache.set size=1.2Gi total=6.6Gi``` repeated.
anne (sre): evidence supporting B: batching_backlog spiked to 200 right before OOM.
ryan (oncall): we should track hypotheses in-thread. H1 (KV cache pinned contiguous allocations) - assigned to maya to validate by replay. H2 (batch backlog concurrent allocations) - assigned to anne to test by sim load + batch knobs. H3 (allocator inefficiency for multi-size chunks) - assigned to eli to test with driver/allocator metrics.
maya (runtime-ml): I'll run a controlled replay of recorded requests with kv-cache on/off to measure fragmentation growth and peak contiguous free block size. ETA 25m.
eli (infra): I'll collect per-allocation histograms from the NV driver and try a small allocator patch (jemalloc-like binning) on a staging node.
anne (sre): meanwhile we should productize short-term mitigations: 1) default per-model kv-cache cap (e.g., 2Gi) 2) auto-disable kv-cache when fragmentation ratio > 0.2 3) limit continuous batch backlog to 50 per pool.
jamie (cust-succ): pushing updated customer note: "We're investigating GPU memory issues impacting generation; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up within 1 hour."
ryan (oncall): timeline so far:
 - 1792345600 ~ first 504 spike seen by alerting
 - 1792345678 incident-bot paged oncall for OOMs
 - 1792345702 kv_cache growth logged on runtime-prod-1
 - 1792345742 model config flip (kv_cache disabled) started
 - 1792345801 pod restart, new instance created and batching reduced
 - 1792345850 error rate dropped significantly

ryan (oncall): logs and snippets uploaded to incident artifact store: https://artifacts.redwood/incident/1792345678
anne (sre): adding a note: we saw one strange stack: ```Allocator::alloc(size=3.2Gi) -> failed despite 4.1Gi free total but largest_free_block=1.1Gi``` — classic fragmentation symptom.
maya (runtime-ml): replay test (kv-cache enabled) shows fragmentation rising steadily after ~200 long-context requests; largest_free_block falls below 1.2Gi. turning kv-cache off prevents that.
eli (infra): allocator patch on staging reduced fragmentation by coalescing smaller bins, but we need deeper driver/allocator work. filing ticket to NV partner.
ryan (oncall): immediate action items (post-incident):
 - short-term: set per-model kv-cache default cap to 2Gi, add auto-disable rule on frag>0.22, cap batch_backlog to 50
 - mid-term: implement allocator-aware KV cache eviction strategy (evict contiguous ranges first) and driver tuning
 - long-term: telemetry + alerting: fragmentation_ratio alert at 0.15 and contiguous_free_block < 1.5Gi alerts

ryan (oncall): who can take the postmortem doc? anne volunteer?
anne (sre): I'll own the incident RCA doc. will gather logs, timeline, hypotheses, and mitigation plan. aim to publish preliminary RCA in 48h.
maya (runtime-ml): I'll add model-side experiments and replay results to RCA.
eli (infra): I'll attach allocator histograms and staging patch results.
jamie (cust-succ): I'll coordinate customer comms and update affected customers after RCA.
ryan (oncall): thanks all. closing incident channel for active mitigation. Please add any stray artifacts to the incident folder. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident automatically marked mitigated at 1792345988 — error rate below threshold for 10m.
